An application has been made to the London Stock Exchange for a block listing of 400,000
new ordinary shares of 3.5p in the Company ("New Ordinary Shares") to be admitted to the Official List and to trading on the London Stock Exchange. The admission is expected to be effective on 28 August 2026. 200,000 New Ordinary Shares will be used to satisfy the allotment of shares pursuant to the vesting of awards from time to time under ASOS Plc Long-Term Incentive Scheme ("ALTIS") and 200,000 New Ordinary Shares will be used to satisfy the allotment of shares pursuant to the vesting of options from time to time under the ASOS Plc Sharesave Plan.
The New Ordinary Shares will be issued fully paid and will rank pari passu in all respects with the existing issued Ordinary Shares of the Company.

latest.title: Disposal of Atlanta fulfilment centre
latest.content:
1 Jul 2026 07:00
RNS Number : 4790K
ASOS PLC
01 July 2026
FOR IMMEDIATE RELEASE
THIS ANNOUNCEMENT CONTAINS INSIDE INFORMATION
1 July 2026
ASOS Plc
Global Online Fashion Destination
"ASOS" or the "Group"
Disposal of Atlanta fulfilment centre for c.£48m;marks completion of non-core asset sale programme
ASOS today announces that it has signed and completed the assignment of the lease of its Atlanta fulfilment centre and the disposal of the associated automation assets (together, the "Transaction"). The lease has been assigned to a global consumer brand and the assets are being purchased by a member of the DHL Group. The Transaction marks a further strengthening of the Group's financial position, with net proceeds of c.£48m (c.$63m) and annual cash cost savings of c.£6m at current exchange rates (c.$8m).
Strategic Rationale: Continued execution of ASOS's Efficient Operating Model
The disposal of the Atlanta fulfilment centre represents a further step in ASOS's programme to strengthen its balance sheet and deliver disciplined capital allocation. The site is non-operational and was fully written down in prior periods, and the Transaction enables the Group to realise value from a non-core asset while continuing to simplify its asset base and improve cash generation.
This disposal builds on a series of actions to improve the Group's financial position, including the refinancing in November 2025, repayment of the 2026 convertible bonds in April 2026 and the disposal of the Lichfield fulfilment centre in May 2026. Net proceeds will be retained to support financial flexibility as ASOS continues to execute its strategy.
Financial Impact
The Transaction has resulted in net sale proceeds of c.£48m, with annual cash savings of c.£6m relating to rent and other occupancy costs. There is also a one-off profit before tax of c.£78m at current exchange rates (c.$103m) after adjustments to associated property liabilities which will be recognised as an adjusting item in the Group's financial results for FY26.
The net proceeds will add to the Group's cash position of £209.5m as at 1 March 2026. Taking into account the c.£67m net proceeds from the disposal of the Lichfield fulfilment centre and the c.£48m net proceeds from the Atlanta Transaction, the pro forma net debt (excluding lease liabilities) position is c.£180m (net debt was c.£295m as at 1 March 2026).
Jose Antonio Ramos, ASOS CEO, said:
"The disposal of Atlanta is another clear demonstration of us delivering on our commitments - strengthening the balance sheet, simplifying the business and maintaining strict discipline in how we allocate capital. Since closing the Atlanta fulfilment centre, we have successfully transitioned to our new US operating model, giving customers access to a broader product assortment from our global inventory. The strength of customer engagement gives us confidence in this approach and reinforces the progress we are making as we execute our strategy and reposition ASOS for long-term, sustainable growth."
The person responsible for arranging the release of this announcement on behalf of the Company is Rishi Sharma, General Counsel and Company Secretary.

company_30s.what_they_do: ASOS sells fashion, beauty and lifestyle products online, mainly to young adults. The platform offers a wide range of branded and private‑label items and has built a global e‑commerce ecosystem.
company_30s.why_they_matter: It is one of the UK’s largest online fashion retailers and a key player in the global e‑commerce market. Its strong brand, large customer base, and established logistics network give it a competitive edge in a space that is still expanding.
company_30s.current_state: The business is in a restructuring phase, trimming physical assets, cutting costs and raising capital to shore up its balance sheet. It is still a high‑growth e‑commerce platform, but cash burn remains a concern while it works to improve margins.

rns_narrative: ASOS is selling non‑core assets such as its Atlanta fulfilment centre to free up cash and focus on core operations.
It has issued new shares and is in the process of refinancing to reduce debt and improve liquidity.
The company is also finalising governance updates and AGM outcomes, signalling a shift toward a leaner, cash‑focused model.

crowd_tape.dominant_theme: Quietly optimistic – a small but engaged group is holding out hope for a turnaround.
crowd_tape.bull_narrative: Bulls point to the asset disposals, capital raise and strong brand as catalysts for a rebound. They see the cost cuts as a path to profitability.
crowd_tape.bear_narrative: Bears warn that ongoing cash burn, inventory excess and supply‑chain fragility could derail the recovery. They also note the heavy reliance on UK and US markets.
crowd_tape.sentiment_shift: The chatter has been steady, with a slight uptick in bullish posts after the Atlanta centre sale, but no dramatic swing yet.

whats_happening_now.attention_check: Google Trends for ASOS is flat – no recent spikes, so a surprise catalyst could still be hidden.

near_term_catalysts: Completion of the refinancing package and the new share issuance to strengthen liquidity.
A positive earnings beat in the next quarterly report or an announcement of a new product line or partnership that drives traffic.
A significant uptick in same‑store sales or conversion rates that signals a shift in customer behaviour.
A volume spike that exceeds the 30‑day average and a breakout above the 200‑day moving average.
expect_next.watch_for: Look for a bullish candle that closes above the 50‑day SMA, a volume surge >30% of the average, and a break above the 200‑day MA. Monitor the debt‑to‑equity ratio after the refinancing and any sign of improved cash flow.
expect_next.timing_regime: The stock appears to be in the early stages of a post‑crash recovery. A tight compression suggests a breakout could happen soon once the catalysts materialise.

buy_vs_sell.bull_case: ASOS sits on a deep crash that has pushed it well below its historic valuation. If the company recovers to the midpoint of its recent low, the upside could be several times the current price. The asset disposals and capital raise reduce risk and set the stage for a rebound, making the mean‑reversion thesis compelling.
buy_vs_sell.bear_case: If the cost cuts fail to translate into revenue growth, margin pressure could return, leading to a further slide and potential liquidity issues. A worst‑case scenario is a continued decline that forces the company into a cash‑burn cycle or even delisting.
buy_vs_sell.risk_reward: Potential loss is limited to the current price, while upside could be 3–4 times that if the stock climbs back toward its 52‑week high. The risk/reward ratio is roughly 1:3–4.

playbook.if_bullish: Enter on a pullback to the 20‑day EMA after a bullish candle closes above the 50‑day SMA. Size the position at 5% of your portfolio and place a stop 10% below the entry to cap downside.
playbook.if_watching: Wait for a volume surge >30% of the 30‑day average, a breakout above the 200‑day MA, and a positive earnings surprise. These signals would confirm the mean‑reversion thesis.
playbook.if_passing: If the company defaults on debt or faces regulatory delisting, exit immediately. No other terminal risks are evident at this time.

ai_insights.bottom_line: ASOS is on a deep crash; a timely refinancing and cost cuts could spark a rebound, offering a high upside with limited downside – a classic contrarian play.
